deviations_from_card: (1) Per the brief, the default mode is replay. `npm run bench` uses the recorded answers and makes no model call. Live mode is opt-in (`-- --live`, operator only, never run here). `--replay <file.json>` lays a fixture over the recorded answers. (2) Per the brief, hint leaks are scored with rules/maths leaks(), the rule hint() gates on. The card's ported poc_hints leaks + assembles are not used. `hints.leaked` scores what the MODEL said: every text call is recorded at the provider seam, re-asks included. `hints.reached` scores what hint() handed the TV, and `hints.reasked` counts re-asks. In case 4, leaked is 2/12 (B fails, exit 1) and reached is 0/12. (3) CRITIC REVISE applied. The 9 queries are parsed as text from vision/poc_retrieval.py QUERIES. Those lines carry only `expect` labels, so an ACCEPT table was added beside them. It is JSON-literal, the ids are checked against TITLES, and it is derived from each label. Where two lessons teach the method, both count: grouping for 2x^2-5x-3 and for the factor item, both substitution lessons, and one-step or Linear equations 1 for x/4+3=8. The two NOT IN LIBRARY queries take []=none. (4) The run-3 replay (corpus.run3) is its own answer set. It is reconstructed from the STUDY-DESK-POC-RESULTS.md section C table, because the printout was not kept. The 9th query, 2x+3=2x+5 -> qsL_5Y8uWPU, follows 'every covered problem to the right lesson'. Case 5 also asserts that an off-list library lesson (jWpiMu5LNdg for 3x-7=11) counts as wrong: 7/9. (5) No recorded model read with positions exists. The replay read is therefore the page's truth, which checks the harness, not a model, and the output and doc say so. (6) sim for the essay page is an edit-distance ratio (>=0.9), not difflib's ratio, whose autojunk distorts paragraphs of 200+ characters. Maths uses the exact port of equations_intact. (7) The card's 'stage 2 repeating stage 1' measure is not built. The lab judged escalation by hand and there is no rule to port. (8) Pages benched: maths and essay, the two data.json pages the phone offers as samples. data.json's Spanish page is not a phone sample. (9) Verdict thresholds as coded: A fails when more than 2 items per page are not exact or not selected ('a few' = 2). B fails when leaked/of > 0.1. C fails when wrong > right. An engine error is never a pass. (10) Guard case 9 was added per the brief: nearestItem equals the phone's old inline loop over a y-sweep of every corpus page, ties and an empty list. Case 9 and the card's GUARD case 8 were red before only because the modules did not exist. (11) lab-corpus throws if data.json's maths items drift from vision/poc_ocr.py MATH.
notes: No Python harness runs here. lab-corpus.cjs reads vision/poc_hints.py PROBLEMS['math'], poc_retrieval.py QUERIES/ACCEPT and poc_ocr.py MATH as TEXT, so their lines must stay JSON-literal (the docstrings now say so). Nothing shells out, so an absent Python cannot break the bench. The .py edits are an ACCEPT constant and docstring lines. All three still parse (py_compile), and nothing else changed in them. The bench pins DESK_DATA_DIR to a fresh mkdtemp under the OS temp dir and removes it on exit. With no transcripts there, pickLesson's bestWindow returns null: the lesson id is scored and embeddings are never exercised, even live. Output keys: {read:{maths,essay:{found,of,exact,selects,cyErr,issues,rule,...},seconds}, hints:{leaked,of,latex,reasked,reached,errors,rule,problems,seconds}, retrieval:{right,of,wrong,errors,seconds}, baseline, verdicts:{A,B,C}, providers:{vision,text}}. Exit codes: 1 = a kill criterion failed, 2 = usage or crash. Phone: the tap now calls nearestItem(page.items, y) from desk/src/lib/desk/select.ts (pure, client-safe). Behaviour is identical and guard 9 pins it. No TV screen changed, so no Playwright capture was needed. The first live run (`npm run bench -- --live`, Ollama + claude-cli, or DESK_TEXT_ENGINE=codex) answers the open question: does the model's reported centre survive the phone's nearest-cy tap the way the ring did (16/16)? Nobody has run it.
